title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
claim: CPL can arise by static coupling when the first coordination sphere itself is chiral, or by dynamic coupling of the Ln ion to ligand-centered transitions even if the coordination polyhedron is achiral; dynamic coupling can produce the larger glum because Ln–ligand covalency is usually small.
explanation: Static coupling mixes opposite-parity 4f and 5d character and weakens if covalency is negligible. Dynamic coupling accounts for the unusually high glum of Cs[Eu(hfbc)4] (about +1.32 to +1.38 on 5D0→7F1) through coupling to β-diketonate π* transitions rather than the near-ideal SAP torsion. J-mixing of 7F2 and 7F3 into 7F1 can also increase μ for 5D0→7F1, raise glum, and invert the CPL sign without a Λ/Δ structural inversion.
scope: Ln(III) complexes whose 4f–4f CPL is interpreted by ligand-field coupling, especially camphorate and β-diketonate Eu(III) species.
conditions: Static coupling requires a chiral first sphere; dynamic coupling is invoked when an achiral polyhedron still shows CPL or when glum exceeds the twist-angle prediction.
caveats: The static-versus-dynamic distinction is a mechanistic interpretation drawn from cited analyses, not a direct measurement in this review. Cs[Eu(hfbc)4] quantum yield remains below about 1%.
